chose: only explicit journal files are gate-grade premise leases; prose paths and backticked symbols remain advisory
over: fail the check for every inferred missing referent
make the entire premise report advisory-only
because: The files field is an author assertion with an exact repository address. Text extraction is necessarily heuristic: a path may be evidence rather than a dependency, and a backticked token may be syntax or prose. A missing explicit address is therefore actionable enough to fail a check, while inferred misses should prompt review without claiming either structural or semantic invalidity.

chose: aggregate unleased decisions as coverage instead of rendering one finding per decision
over: render every unleased decision with an action to add files
because: The first dogfood audit produced 64 rows, roughly forty of which merely repeated that an old decision had no extractable address. Absence is useful as a coverage count but supplies no stale referent to investigate; expanding it makes the real missing and ambiguous addresses harder to see. Actionable rows are therefore reserved for leases whose state can actually be classified.
